claim: A pure psychometric/IRT benchmark-auditing paper (PSN-IRT), applied across 11 existing LLM benchmarks with no new task/domain contribution, was accepted as an AAAI 2026 Oral.
stance_target: AAAI venue-fit for a psychometric/IRT-based benchmark diagnostic artifact paper
scope_conditions: AAAI 2026 acceptance, 11 mainstream LLM benchmarks, 41,871 items
quoted_support: Accepted to AAAI 2026 (Oral)... we conduct extensive analysis on 11 LLM benchmarks comprising 41,871 items, revealing significant and varied shortcomings in their measurement quality.

claim: PSN-IRT demonstrates that IRT-selected smaller benchmark subsets retain stronger alignment with human preference than naive subsetting, establishing a constructive payoff pattern (diagnostic finding + smaller reliable benchmark) for IRT benchmark papers.
stance_target: the constructive-payoff pattern needed for an AAAI-viable benchmark/diagnostic artifact paper
quoted_support: we demonstrate that leveraging PSN-IRT is able to construct smaller benchmarks while maintaining stronger alignment with human preference.

claim: PSN-IRT operates at whole-benchmark-item granularity across general LLM benchmarks and does not address code-generation benchmarks or sub-task/unit-test-level requirement structure.
stance_target: novelty of requirement-level IRT specifically for code benchmarks
quoted_support: This paper provides a critical analysis of benchmark effectiveness, examining mainstream prominent LLM benchmarks using results from diverse models.
